Original DESIGN.md and TRIGGER.txt hashes remain unchanged. Revised trigger contains 3974 characters.

Recomputed all 181 captured section hashes and all 190 chunk hashes and contiguous coverage ranges successfully. Eight heading-only gRPC bodies are accurately marked read-source-gap. Card text contains 42 page separators; inventory records pages 0–41.
Verified acquisition receipt and selected local-document capture hashes and sizes. Installed local guides match their captures.

Original acceptance/resource obligations remain incorporated, including full SP01–SP12/MC01–MC08, financial/native/Preview gates, historical charges, failure stops and three-consecutive-goal-turn blocked rule.
Latest Grok implementation and separate fresh Opus/Astra review routing is explicit. Existing-goal steering prohibits false completion, recreation and duplicate scheduling.

Review prompts require substantive independent exact-byte verdicts, returned identities and re-audits after changes. Canary success is correctly separated from design/product approval.

Inspected sanitized Grok canaries and root smoke verification receipt. Requested grok-4.6 and observed grok-4.6-build remain distinct; private reasoning is excluded and unknown accounting remains unknown.
Guarded status failed with sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file. Next returned sp01-loan-report with unresolved admission/history evidence. No dispatch followed.
Read-only live Grok version/help returned grok 1.0.25 (f7e67d6988e2), differing from the captured 1.0.13 observation.

findings.requirement: Describe actual permission behavior without claiming a closed allowlist that the installed documentation does not establish.
findings.consequence: The assertion that unmatched actions in dontAsk fail omits built-in automatic approvals. The captured permissions guide explicitly allows read-only tools and recognized shell commands without matching allow rules, including under dontAsk. Scoped Read/Bash rules therefore do not establish the stated boundary by themselves.
findings.repair: Qualify the assertion with built-in automatic approvals and merged configuration rules. Preserve the existing host containment requirement and scoped commands; do not add broad grants or new infrastructure.

findings.requirement: Ground CLI behavior in the cited captured evidence and distinguish untested behavior from established behavior.
findings.consequence: The claim that headless --worktree does not create a worktree 'per installed help' is unsupported. Captured help describes creating a new worktree, and raw/local-14-headless-mode.md:672 explicitly describes worktree creation among headless flags. DESIGN.md:47 and TRIGGER.txt:7 repeat the unsupported categorical claim.
findings.repair: Retain the chosen pre-created checkout plus --cwd approach. Replace the categorical claim with an accurate statement that automatic headless worktree behavior was not validated by these canaries, and cite the documented behavior without claiming runtime verification.

limits: Inventory integrity and coverage were independently verified; author-reported historical reading activity cannot be proven from the inventory alone. I inspected relevant primary-source bodies, not every corpus body or all card pages anew.
Current Grok 1.0.25 runtime execution was not canary-tested. Historical 1.0.13 documentation and invocation evidence must not be presented as observed execution of the current binary.
Native goal state, scheduler liveness and host interception were not independently observed.
Historical Opus invocation outcomes were supplied by the user; I did not reopen the historical substantive K review or any other current design-review verdict.
No source edits, delegation, goal mutation, provider calls, K/native/prover/service/wallet/public actions or publication occurred.
This review establishes no roadmap, financial, proof, ledger or product completion.

reviewerIdentity.observedProviderModel: Not independently exposed in this review context; parent must bind the actual host model and effort metadata.
